definition: An unsupervised neural network (Kohonen map) that projects high-dimensional data onto a low-dimensional grid while preserving topology — used for visualization and clustering.
details: An unsupervised neural network (Kohonen map) that projects high-dimensional data onto a low-dimensional grid while preserving topology — used for visualization and clustering.

explainer.lead: Self-organizing maps, or Kohonen maps, are unsupervised neural networks that project high-dimensional data onto a low-dimensional grid while preserving topology. They matter for visualization and clustering.

tiers.eli5: Think of a stretching sheet that bends itself so similar items end up next to each other on a grid.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers use them for topology-preserving projection of high-dimensional data into a grid for visualization and clustering. A pitfall is reading cluster positions as precise distances rather than a topology-preserving layout.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, it is an unsupervised neural network (Kohonen map) that projects high-dimensional data onto a low-dimensional grid while preserving topology. Its known use is visualization and clustering.

explainer.example: Customers described by many attributes are placed on a 2D grid, with similar customers forming neighboring regions for clustering.
